summary: This paper presents a method to estimate circuit-level noise for surface-code QEC by analyzing repeated plaquette measurements under two ancilla strategies: FRESH (fresh syndrome qubits per round) and RECYCLE (reused syndrome qubit). The approach extracts effective plaquette error rates, idle errors, and time-correlated errors from single-shot measurement statistics without requiring access to low-level gate calibrations.
motivation: On near-term quantum computers with cloud access or large-scale deployments, detailed gate-level calibration is often unavailable, yet noise models are essential for predicting QEC code performance. Shuttling-based architectures (ion traps, neutral atoms) introduce reuse-dependent correlation effects not captured by standard metrics, necessitating a circuit-level extraction method.
method: Two syndrome-qubit configurations execute plaquette circuits with varying repetition depths on IonQ Aria1 (trapped-ion) and IBM Torino (superconducting). FRESH uses $n$ separate syndrome qubits while RECYCLE uses one; measurement probabilities $p_x$ and $p_{x,y}$ are fit to error model equations to isolate $p_	ext{plaq}$, $c_	ext{orre}$ (time-like correlated error), $i_	ext{dle}$, and $m_	ext{ea}$ (measurement error). For IonQ, hardware-aware rewrite templates reduce circuit depth via GPI2 gate cancellations and commutations with Mølmer–Sørensen gates.
result: On IonQ Aria1, optimized Plaquette-3 achieves $p_	ext{plaq} \approx 1.5\%$ (down from $3.0\%$ for Plaquette-1), reducing circuit depth by roughly 50% through native-gate optimization. On IBM Torino, negative $c_	ext{orre}$ values indicate the RECYCLE–FRESH difference is dominated by routing overhead in fixed-connectivity layouts, suggesting the model is most applicable to shuttling platforms where reuse induces genuine time-correlated effects.
